headline: LLM agents and constrained annotation anchor spatial omics analysis to expert knowledge
label: Computational Spatial Transcriptomics Methods
summary: Recent items pair LLM agents, foundation models and curated marker or pathway knowledge with spatial and single-cell omics analysis.
synthesis: The dominant thread is anchoring computational analysis of spatial and single-cell omics to external knowledge, including curated marker vocabularies, pathway knowledge and foundation-model embeddings. NanoCellAnnotator and an ambiguity-aware multi-stage framework constrain LLM cell-type labels to PanglaoDB and CellMarker vocabularies with confidence flags, and SPEAK prompts LLMs with neighbor-cell markers for tissue domain identification. SP-Mind applies an autonomous LLM agent across spatial proteomics workflows, from raw tissue imaging to phenotype discovery, and introduces the SP-Bench benchmark. Histopathology-to-expression work aligns frozen histopathology and RNA-seq foundation models for open-vocabulary gene-set prompting, and ResSAT predicts spatial transcriptomic profiles from H&E images. What is new is constrained LLM inference paired with spatial and marker-based evidence, though this is not universal across the set. FICUS, DSEN and GR-SAFS address network modeling and biomarker selection with less direct spatial emphasis.
